abstract.t:
HTTP provides a suite of requests and responses for communicating changes to resource state, but they are limited in symmetry and reproducibility. PATCH is sent client-to-server, but a server cannot send a PATCH to a client. POST can change server state flexibly, but its behavior is server-defined, and cannot be reproduced by a naive server, client, or intermediary.
This document extends ordinary HTTP requests and responses into a suite of symmetric, reproducible *updates*. A sequence of updates can be replayed on any client, server, or intermediary to reproduce identical changes to state.
There are three types of updates: snapshots, patches, and deletions, and this document defines how they occur symmetrically in both requests and responses. Arbitrary patch formats can be defined with a new Patch-Type header, but most patches can be expressed as a replacement of a range expressed via an extended syntax of Range Unit.
This document is one of the Braid-HTTP extensions, which work alone or together; together they make HTTP a state synchronization protocol.
